subject: AI & Agents
title: Reasoning Models: AI That Thinks Longer
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Reasoning Models: AI That Thinks Longer.

hook.text: What if AI could pause and think for minutes before answering, like a human solving a hard problem?

buildup.text: Reasoning models like o1 use extended chain-of-thought before producing a final answer.

discovery.text: They break complex problems into sub-problems and verify each step internally.

twist.text: More thinking time costs more compute and money. Reasoning has a literal price.

climax.text: On PhD-level science and math, reasoning models dramatically outperform standard LLMs.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best answer just takes longer to find.

quiz.question: How do reasoning models like o1 improve accuracy?
options: By using extended chain-of-thought to break down complex problems
By accessing larger training datasets at inference time

details.summary: Reasoning models use extended inference time to work through complex problems step by step. Unlike standard LLMs that answer immediately, they generate longer internal reasoning chains before producing higher-quality answers.
details.whyItMatters: Reasoning models show that spending more compute at inference — not just training — dramatically improves accuracy. This opens a new axis for improving AI beyond simply making models larger.
takeaways: Reasoning models trade speed for accuracy on complex problems
They generate internal reasoning chains before final answers
Inference-time compute is a new scaling axis for AI capability

faq.question: How do reasoning models differ from standard LLMs?
faq.answer: Standard LLMs produce tokens at constant speed. Reasoning models allocate more computation to harder problems, generating extended chains of thought. The result is slower but significantly more accurate on complex tasks.

faq.question: What problems benefit from reasoning models?
faq.answer: Math competitions, complex coding, scientific reasoning, and multi-step logic problems see the biggest improvements. For simple questions or creative writing, standard LLMs are faster without meaningful accuracy loss.
